def factor_value_small_size_quality_filter(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    # Book yield cheapness
    cheapness = 1.0 / df_copy["pb_lf"].replace(0, np.nan)
    # Time-series size regime: rolling median of mkt_cap_float (1 year window)
    size_median = df_copy["mkt_cap_float"].rolling(252, min_periods=63).median()
    # Flag small: current mkt_cap_float below rolling median
    is_small = df_copy["mkt_cap_float"] < size_median
    # Quality filter: positive ROE
    positive_roe = df_copy["roe_ttm2"] > 0
    # For small caps, use cheapness only if ROE positive; for large caps, use cheapness as is
    df_copy["factor_value_small_size_quality_filter"] = np.where(
        is_small & ~positive_roe, np.nan, cheapness
    )
    return df_copy["factor_value_small_size_quality_filter"]
formula: PB_cheapness = 1 / pb_lf; if mkt_cap_float < rolling_median(mkt_cap_float, 252) AND roe_ttm2 <= 0 then nan else PB_cheapness
rationale: Value signals (book yield) are conditioned on size by applying a quality filter (positive ROE) only for stocks in a time-series small-cap regime (current float market cap below its 1-year rolling median). This avoids amplifying distressed small-cap value traps while preserving the cheapness signal for large caps. The mechanism uses size as a conditional gate, not a monotonic multiplier.
